text:
marta: Heads up — noticed a 12% tail-latency bump on route /v1/generate starting ~04:00 UTC. Dashboards show token-level spikes in 'kv_lookup' and 'kernel_switch' buckets. cc @lee @ashok :warning:
lee: saw that alert. Which model and quantization profile? Any correlation with batch sizes? :thinking:
marta: It's the rwd-v2-medium quantized-q4f. Most traffic 1-4 tokens/sec, but we had a small spike of long-seq requests (seq=1024) that coincided. Batching median stayed the same but P95 batch size increased from 4->9.
ashok: could be kernel selection thrashing when sequence length distribution suddenly shifts. If the runtime switches kernels mid-request or picks a non-optimal matmul kernel that increases KV decode time, token latency rises. Do we have traces for individual slow requests?
ci-bot: New trace samples uploaded: trace_id=trc_20260318_abc123, trc_20260318_def456 (uploaded at 1852100020). :white_check_mark:
sana: grabbed trc_20260318_abc123 — I see repeated kernel-switch events around token 342 and 347. KV cache hit rate also drops to ~62% for that request window (normally ~89%). Looks like partial KV invalidation.
lee: partial KV invalidation? Do we have any code paths that evict prefixes during batching changes?
marta: Not intentionally. But the trace shows kv_invalidate events right after a batching re-group op. Possible race in batching heuristic when mixing short+long requests causing partial cache scope mismatch.
ashok: if batching groups requests with different past_lengths, the runtime may shard KV caches per-batch and attempt a prefix trim. Might produce an extra memcpy + re-populate, which would show as extra ms in kv_lookup and also trigger a kernel variant that expects cold KV.
zack: attaching the short profiler snippet I ran on the instance: ```
# perf snapshot (simplified)
kv_lookup: 18.4ms
attn_kernel_matmul_fast: 6.2ms
attn_kernel_matmul_fallback: 14.9ms
kernel_switch_overhead: 4.6ms
net_send: 1.2ms
```
lee: that fallback kernel time is suspicious — fallback should only kick in for >2048 seq or unsupported shapes. Why did it choose fallback for 1024? Any kernel feature flags flipped at 04:00?
sana: ops deploy at 03:58 pushed a binary with a scalar change to kernel selection logic (PR #4123). The release notes mention an adjustment to prefer the new fused-attn for some shapes. Could be mis-routed shapes.
marta: linking dashboard panels: Token latency breakdown panel: https://dash.internal/rwd/runtime/token_breakdown?route=/v1/generate&since=04:00 (P95 kv_lookup spike). Per-route KPI: https://dash.internal/rwd/runtime/route_kpis?route=/v1/generate
lee: can we reproduce locally by replaying a sample from the slow trace with original binary vs previous binary? If kernel selection is the culprit it should reproduce deterministically.
zack: replay script I used: ```python
# replay snippet
client.send_requests(batch=[..], seq_lengths=[32, 1024, 16, 1024])
``` worked to reproduce the kernel_switch pattern on a dev instance when I toggled the new kernel flag off. With flag OFF, fallback kernel not picked and kv hit rate stays 88%.
ashok: that suggests the new selection heuristic mis-classifies some shapes and forces a kernel that doesn't handle our KV layout efficiently. Two actions: revert selection heuristic in next canary, and add a unit test that replays mixed short+long batches.
sana: agreed. I'm rolling a hotfix to canary group now and will watch the token_breakdown panel. Rolling back flag to previous behavior for canary only. Patch: roll/flag/kernel_sel=off on canary.
ci-bot: Canaries updated: canary-1, canary-2 at 1852100048. Health checks green.
marta: after canary roll-back P95 on /v1/generate normalized within 8 minutes. KV hit rate back to 90±2%. P95 token latency back to baseline. :tada:
lee: follow-ups: 1) add regression test in perf suite for mixed-length batching; 2) add a dashboard alert when P95 token-level kv_lookup increases by >7% vs 1h baseline; 3) instrument kernel choice in traces (add kernel_id annotation).
sana: I'll file the jira and assign. jira: RWD-9876 (perf/regression - kernel selection in mixed batches).
zack: also recommend adding a cheap sampler that logs batch composition histograms per 5m — helps detect distribution shifts before they hit P95.
marta: thanks everyone. I'll add a short runbook entry to incidents playbook: what to check (kv_hit_rate, kernel_switch counts, batch_size histogram, recent kernel selection flags) and link common remediation (toggle flag, revert PR).
lee: nice triage. tagging this thread for postmortem notes. :memo: 
ci-bot: thread archived and linked to RWD-9876 at 1852100065.
